BiblicalUsage: Mikmethath is a place on the border of Ephraim's allotment, named twice as Joshua marks out the land. It stands on the north side of the boundary, facing Shechem, and its name survives only in those two boundary lists.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the boundary stones matter: God gave His people a real land with real borders, and even a name that appears only twice is part of the inheritance He measured out.
